correctness.rationale: For any odd prime, Loukaki Theorem A certifies mixed/mixed minors (after parity translation); pure/mixed and pure/pure reduce to prime-order Chebotarev. Prime-coordinate collision forces precisely two proportional columns (or rows), with rank two from a nonzero 2x2 prime Fourier minor. The disjoint pure/collision cases have A=2C(p,3), B=2p(p−1), yielding 2AB singular minors. Three-frequency mixed-parity support has at most two zeros; pure support gives 0,2,4 paired zeros. Explicit constructions realize all values and an order-2p cubic gives the sharp 2p−3 exact-support Fourier bound. Exact determinant enumeration passed for p=3,5,7. These finite computations do not prove the universal assertion.

value.rationale: A complete all-prime, rank-stratified classification of the first nontrivial nonprincipal Fourier-minor defects is a natural sampling/interpolation invariant. The exact count and uniform three-frequency zero spectrum isolate an absent stratum not encoded by ordinary at-most-support uncertainty, yielding a sharp natural exact-support invariant for every p>=5. This structural consequence is more substantial than a trivial numerical recomputation.
